title: What's in the Bigfoot Files?
excerpt: We take a look at the mystery of Bigfoot, after some old government files were released.
content:
BIGFOOT
First up, to a long-standing mystery, which is back in the spotlight. Involving a creature with very big feet. For decades, people have been on the hunt for a giant, hairy, upright-walking ape-like creature, called Bigfoot. The name 'Bigfoot' first became famous after reports of giant footprints were published in a newspaper in 1958, and in 1967 we got our first alleged vision of the mysterious creature. While skeptics think it was probably just someone in a costume, it inspired a wave of Bigfoot hunters. Even the FBI, the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation, got involved. The search for Bigfoot is serious business. And now, we have fresh info on the guy. The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Forest Service recently made three old government files public, covering separate incidents across US states: Montana and Oregon. These included a six-page report recounting a 1940s hunting trip. A 2003 newspaper article about reported human-like or possible Bigfoot tracks. And a 1982 U.S. Department of Agriculture report, which investigated alleged Bigfoot tracks. The report concluded that the tracks studied probably weren't made by a giant ape-like creature. Though they did say that if they were faked, someone certainly went to a lot of trouble. So yeah, the new files don't necessarily solve the Bigfoot mystery. They have certainly reignited it.

COP 31
COP31 has ended without a deal! This year's UN climate summit was led by Australia and Türkiye, but the deal they put forward was rejected. Talks broke down over a draft that was considered too weak by several countries because it didn't mention fossil fuels... like coal, oil and gas. Debate went two days over time, making this the longest UN climate summit ever!

F1
It was a drama-filled Las Vegas Grand Prix, with the lead changing hands 35 times! Red Bull's Max Verstappen started in pole position, while McLaren's Oscar Piastri began all the way back in 17th. After some back-and-forth, Mercedes' George Russell retook the spot on Lap 28. But Verstappen managed to take back the lead, while George Russell crashed into a wall. In the end, Max Verstappen won by just six tenths of a second, while McLaren's Lando Norris narrowly took second place, and Oscar Piastri charged through to third.

AFLW
Speaking of impressive wins, both the North Melbourne Kangaroos and the Melbourne Demons have secured their spots in this year's AFLW Grand Final. The Demons came out swinging. While Carlton put up a good fight. The Blues were no match for Melbourne, who cruised to a 30 point win. It was the same story for the North Melbourne Kangaroos, who held off the Sydney Swans to win 83 to 51.

MOTO GP
And finally, to Portugal, where Ducati's Marc Marquez has been crowned the 2026 MotoGP Champion. He actually finished eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix, but he only needed to place in the top nine to secure the championship! It's his 8th MotoGP title!

BULLDOG PHOTO
First up, to hundreds of bulldogs in Mexico City. Everyone here has turned out to take a big group photo together! They're trying to set a new world record for the largest bulldog photo session in the world. They reckon they've almost got 800 here. But we don't know if they've made it just yet, the attempt is still in the process of being counted and verified.

HIGH HEELS
Now to a high heel race in China! Who can run 100 metres the fastest, while wearing stilettos at least 7 centimetres high. Amazingly, I can't see anyone falling over!

GUINEA PIGS
And finally! To guinea pigs in Bolivia getting all dressed up. This is the guinea pig fair, celebrating Andean traditions, and the important role guinea pigs play in everyday life. There was even a mock guinea pig wedding.
